payload.task_text:
Our team uses a popular tech education channel for ongoing developer learning. I need a monthly digest of content published in the first half of 2025 to help our team stay current on trending tech topics.

From our video database, retrieve all videos from the Fireship channel published between January 2025 and June 2025 inclusive. For each calendar month in that range, identify the single top video by view count.

Create a presentation file called Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx in your workspace. The presentation must have a title slide with the exact title text "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest" and then one content slide for each of the six months (January through June 2025), for a total of seven slides. Each monthly slide must use the month and year as the slide title (for example "January 2025"). The body content of each monthly slide must include all four of the following pieces of information: the top video title for that month, the view count formatted as a plain integer, the video duration converted to minutes and rounded to one decimal place, and the total count of videos published by the channel in that month.

Schedule a monthly review meeting in the shared calendar for each of the six months. Use these exact dates and times: 2025-01-07 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-02-04 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-03-04 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-04-01 from 09:00 to 09:30, 2025-05-06 from 09:00 to 09:30, and 2025-06-03 from 09:00 to 09:30. Use the America/New_York timezone for all calendar events in this task. Each event title must follow the exact pattern "Monthly Tech Digest Review - [Month Year]" where Month Year is the full month name and year such as "January 2025". Each event description must mention the title of the top video for that month.

Send an email to team@company.com with the subject line "Fireship 2025 Monthly Digest Ready". The email body must list all six monthly top videos, each including the video title and its view count. Ensure all six months from January through June 2025 are represented in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one wave with exactly one Coder sub-agent. That agent should keep the complete channel scan, six monthly selections, and presentation together; a separate source wave would add a redundant handoff.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent to own one complete read-only Fireship channel catalog session and `Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx`. Obtain one channel list identifier, navigate the returned list identifier sequentially at the maximum supported page size until an empty page or source exhaustion, and preserve Video_ID, full title, published timestamp, integer view count, and duration. Filter locally to January 1 through June 30, 2025 inclusive. For each of the six calendar months, count all candidates and choose the single highest-view video with a stable Video_ID tie-break; report a source-empty month rather than inventing one. Convert duration to minutes once. Create one presentation identifier and exactly seven slides: the exact title plus six chronological month slides, each containing all four required values. Read the deck back and return path, compact six-month table, channel page/row/date/ranking controls, and slide count/content checks.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates all six selections, then issues six `list_events` calls natively in parallel using narrow ISO ranges around the original slots and sufficient `maxResults`; inspect exact title/time locally. Issue only missing `create_event` calls natively in parallel with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime`, `timeZone="America/New_York"` in both objects, exact titles, and that month's verified top-video title in its description. Retrieve each returned/reused ID with `get_event`. Only after deck and event inventory agree, check Sent mail and send one missing exact-recipient/subject email listing all six month/title/integer-view pairs. Read it back and finish without another wave.

Build a PowerPoint presentation and save it to the exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-ppt-gcal-email/workspace/Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx

Use the pptx MCP server tools (mcp__pptx__create_presentation, mcp__pptx__add_slide, mcp__pptx__populate_placeholder / mcp__pptx__add_bullet_points, mcp__pptx__save_presentation, etc.) to construct the deck. It must contain EXACTLY 7 slides:

Slide 1 (title slide): title text exactly "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest" (nothing else required).

Slides 2–7 (one per month). Each slide's title must be exactly the month and year (e.g. "January 2025"). The body content of each slide must include ALL FOUR of these pieces of information: the top video title for that month, the view count as a plain integer (no commas, no formatting), the video duration converted to minutes and rounded to one decimal place, and the total count of videos published by the channel in that month. Use exactly the data below (already verified):

- Slide 2, title "January 2025": top video title "Big Tech in panic mode... Did DeepSeek R1 just pop the AI bubble?"; view count 3878491; duration 3.6 minutes; total videos published 9.
- Slide 3, title "February 2025": top video title "Microsoft's new chip looks like science fiction…" (note the unicode ellipsis character … at the end); view count 2329914; duration 4.3 minutes; total videos published 9.
- Slide 4, title "March 2025": top video title "The \"vibe coding\" mind virus explained…" (unicode ellipsis …); view count 1846051; duration 4.8 minutes; total videos published 9.
- Slide 5, title "April 2025": top video title "7 Programming myths that waste your time"; view count 1525851; duration 6.3 minutes; total videos published 6.
- Slide 6, title "May 2025": top video title "Google goes wild, again... 11 things you missed at I/O"; view count 1395286; duration 4.5 minutes; total videos published 6.
- Slide 7, title "June 2025": top video title "Google's new CLI tool hits different…" (unicode ellipsis …); view count 1066444; duration 4.2 minutes; total videos published 7.

Suggested body layout per monthly slide (bullet points or labeled lines):
- Top Video: <title>
- Views: <plain integer>
- Duration: <X.X> minutes
- Videos Published: <integer>

Acceptance criteria: the file /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-ppt-gcal-email/workspace/Fireship_2025_Digest.pptx exists and is a valid .pptx with exactly 7 slides; slide 1 title is exactly "Fireship 2025 Monthly Tech Digest"; each monthly slide title is exactly the month+year; each monthly slide contains the 4 data points with the exact values above. After saving, verify the file exists (e.g. mcp__filesystem__get_file_info) and report the final path and slide count in your conclusion.
Build Fireship 2025 digest PPTX

Perform two external-write tasks. Use the Google Calendar MCP tools (mcp__google_calendar__create_event) and the email MCP tools (mcp__emails__send_email).

TASK A — Create 6 calendar events in the shared Google Calendar. All events must use timezone America/New_York, run 09:00–09:30 local time on the given dates. Each event title must follow the exact pattern "Monthly Tech Digest Review - [Month Year]" (e.g. "Monthly Tech Digest Review - January 2025"). Each event description must mention the top video title for that month (use the titles given below). Create exactly these 6 events:

1. Date 2025-01-07, title "Monthly Tech Digest Review - January 2025", description must mention: Big Tech in panic mode... Did DeepSeek R1 just pop the AI bubble?
2. Date 2025-02-04, title "Monthly Tech Digest Review - February 2025", description must mention: Microsoft's new chip looks like science fiction… (unicode ellipsis character)
3. Date 2025-03-04, title "Monthly Tech Digest Review - March 2025", description must mention: The "vibe coding" mind virus explained… (unicode ellipsis character)
4. Date 2025-04-01, title "Monthly Tech Digest Review - April 2025", description must mention: 7 Programming myths that waste your time
5. Date 2025-05-06, title "Monthly Tech Digest Review - May 2025", description must mention: Google goes wild, again... 11 things you missed at I/O
6. Date 2025-06-03, title "Monthly Tech Digest Review - June 2025", description must mention: Google's new CLI tool hits different… (unicode ellipsis character)

Use start dateTime "YYYY-MM-DDT09:00:00" and end dateTime "YYYY-MM-DDT09:30:00" with timeZone "America/New_York" for each event. Example: start {"dateTime": "2025-01-07T09:00:00", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, end {"dateTime": "2025-01-07T09:30:00", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.

TASK B — Send ONE email:
- To: team@company.com
- Subject (exact): Fireship 2025 Monthly Digest Ready
- Body: must list all SIX monthly top videos, each including the video title and its view count (plain integers as given). Include all six months January through June 2025. Suggested format (plain text):
January 2025: Big Tech in panic mode... Did DeepSeek R1 just pop the AI bubble? — 3878491 views
February 2025: Microsoft's new chip looks like science fiction… — 2329914 views
March 2025: The "vibe coding" mind virus explained… — 1846051 views
April 2025: 7 Programming myths that waste your time — 1525851 views
May 2025: Google goes wild, again... 11 things you missed at I/O — 1395286 views
June 2025: Google's new CLI tool hits different… — 1066444 views
(You may add a brief intro/outro line, but all six entries above must be present with title and view count.)

Acceptance criteria: 6 calendar events created with the exact titles and correct dates/times/timezone, each description mentioning its month's top video title; 1 email sent to team@company.com with the exact subject and a body containing all six monthly top videos with titles and view counts. In your conclusion, report the event IDs returned for each calendar event and the email send result.
